chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I had lunch with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he brought a sand grouse and said: 'It is blessed.' My father (peace be upon him) was fond of it, and he used to instruct that the sufferer of jaundice be fed with it, grilled for him, for it benefits him.
ai.seo_question: What is the medicinal benefit of sand grouse according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s appreciation for the medicinal properties of sand grouse (*Qat*), specifically its efficacy in treating jaundice (*Yaraqan*), a practice rooted in the tradition of his father, Imam al-Baqir. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *Tibb al-Nabawi* (Prophetic Medicine), where specific foods are prescribed for their therapeutic benefits, blending spiritual blessing (*Barakah*) with practical health wisdom.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Mahziyar who said,

‘I had lunch with Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> came with a sand grouse, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is Blessed and my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was fascinated by it, and he<sup>asws</sup> used to instruct the sufferer of jaundice to be fed with it, grilled for him, so he would benefit by it’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn Mahziyar from who has said the following: “

I once had lunch with abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and sand grouse was brought. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is blessed; my father liked it and would instruct to feed roasted to one who suffers from jaundice; it benefits him.’”
